\section{Introduction}
We classify literal linear generalized Stone--Wales paths in the
Goldberg--Coxeter images of the dodecahedron. The endpoint condition
must hold before the first repeated surface vertex. The proof reduces
this comparison to two arithmetic stages, with positive belt witnesses
and explicit collisions for the negative cases. The constructions and
path definition come from the cited fullerene literature; the exact
novelty comparison is discussed in Section~\ref{sec:review}.

\section{What is proved, and how}\label{sec:guarantees}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{p{.22\textwidth}p{.28\textwidth}p{.38\textwidth}}
\toprule Claim & Present proof basis & Scope\\\midrule
Theorem~\ref{thm:classification} & Lean graph theorem and prose geometric proofs & All integer $k>l>0$, including nonprimitive parameters; explicit closed surface quotient.\\
Corollary~\ref{cor:minimum} & Lean graph and bounded arithmetic theorem & Primitive $k>l>0$, with the minimum at $(17,5)$.\\
Corollary~\ref{cor:rays} & Lean existence theorem; prose threshold arithmetic & Every eventually interior integer affine ray, including nonprimitive points; the executable threshold/period algorithm remains an obligation.\\
Corollary~\ref{cor:density} & Prose counting proof draft & Primitive parameter points, with its stated counting and limit obligations.\\
Finite checks and census & Explicit constructors, path searches and absence-certificate checkers & The ranges in Section~\ref{sec:checks} and Appendix~\ref{app:census}; separate full-code comparison through $C_{186}$.\\
Auxiliary formal claims & Lean arithmetic and conditional graph propositions & Exact hypotheses and types in the claim ledger.\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Two separately developed prose derivations cover the full interior A3
classification. The formal claims concern the specified quotient graph;
its interpretation as the intended published construction and human
proof peer review remain distinct matters. The priority comparison is
open. The supplementary \record{VERIFICATION-RECORD.md} records roles,
independence qualifications, formal entry points and validation history.

\section{Correspondence with Lean (P001/P002)}\label{sec:lean}
\subsection{Exact graph specification and completed conclusions}
The fixed environment is Lean 4.35.0 and mathlib v4.35.0. The
coordinator wrote an independent specification using only mathlib:
twenty oriented parent faces on twelve labels, integer lattice points
of closed triangles, and equivalence generated by edge gluings.
The simple graph \record{ClaudeChallenge.gcGraph} defines adjacency
from lattice triangles, and \record{LiteralPath} uses actual neighbour
sets, distinct vertices and an even number of vertices. Internal
degree-five vertices are allowed. The arithmetic predicate
\record{ClaudeChallenge.criterion} includes $\gcd(k,l)=1$ and the
alternatives in (2). Domain assumptions are $k,l\in\mathbb N$,
$0<l<k$; positive integer inputs correspond to the paper's domain.

The research team's surface descriptions are connected by proved
graph isomorphisms to this independent quotient. In the nonprimitive
case the closed model retains ordinary lattice vertices on parent
edges. Degree five is proved equivalent to being a parent vertex,
and other vertices have degree six. The argument derives local
triangle continuation, coherent chart changes and a finite lift of
every literal path. It is not conditional on an unproved development
certificate. Primitive necessity uses the start reduction and sector
collisions; the coordinator's positive construction supplies the
converse. The resulting theorem is
\record{ClaudeMain.main_full} in
\record{formal/Formal/ClaudeMainFull.lean}:
\[
 (\exists n,p,\ \operatorname{LiteralPath}(\operatorname{gcGraph}(k,l),n,p))
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{criterion}(k,l).
\]
There is no primitivity hypothesis in this theorem. The declaration
\record{ClaudeMain.main_primitive} is its earlier primitive checkpoint.
The full declaration proves the independent challenge's statement
\record{ClaudeChallenge.main}; it does not add an axiom with that name.

For Corollary~\ref{cor:minimum},
\record{ClaudeCor.minimum_at} proves that among primitive $k>l>0$
with $T\le399$, absence is equivalent to $(k,l)=(17,5)$.
\record{minimum_negative}, \record{minimum_below} and
\record{minimum_data} record absence, existence below the bound,
primitivity and the norm calculation. The bounded arithmetic table
uses kernel \record{decide}, not native evaluation.

For Corollary~\ref{cor:rays}, \record{ClaudeCor.criterion_ray}
proves existence of a threshold and a positive period on every
integer affine ray eventually satisfying $0<l(t)<k(t)$.
\record{R002.A3Release.path_ray} transports this to literal-path
existence using the full classification, including nonprimitive
points. The parameter $t$ is natural, which describes the same
positive tail as sufficiently large integer $t$. No executable
algorithm computing the threshold and period is certified. Therefore
the entire wording of Corollary~\ref{cor:rays} retains a partial
formalization obligation. Corollary~\ref{cor:density} remains outside
the formalization target. No formal proof of the Python or C solver,
the census generators, or the order formula is inferred.

\subsection{Axioms, reproducibility and Comparator scope}
The packet includes the Lean source dependency closure, the pinned
toolchain and manifest, and \record{Formal/A3ReleaseCheck.lean}.
The latter reprints axiom dependencies and runs an automatic
allowlist gate accepting only \record{propext},
\record{Classical.choice} and \record{Quot.sound} transitively.
It rejects unfinished proofs, custom axioms and native-evaluation
trust axioms. Reproduction instructions and exact records are in
\record{FORMALIZATION.md} and \record{formalization.json}; mathlib
caches are excluded. The four small Python packet checks inspect
saved types and outputs; they are not a Lean execution.

The coordinator's Comparator challenge copies its independently
written definitions and has a deliberately unproved target statement.
The submitted solution is \record{ClaudeMain.main_full}.
Comparator checks the equality of the challenge statement and the
proved statement, with the three-axiom allowlist. The full-theorem
run recorded acceptance by Lean's standard and paranoid kernels,
lean4lean, nanoda, con-leche and con-ron. The six kernels check the
same formal proof; they are not six independent mathematical reviews.
That run covers the full classification, including nonprimitive
parameters, but not the later minimum and ray proofs. The earlier
primitive Comparator run has its separate scope and logs.
The macOS runs explicitly disabled the unavailable Linux sandbox;
they do not establish process isolation. The fixed reports and raw
outputs are supplied, without claiming a new six-kernel run in v7.

An independent specification and a proved graph isomorphism reduce
the risk of proving a convenient surrogate. They do not prove that
the specification expresses the intended published definition or
that every coordinate formula in the prose is a transcription of
the formal proof. On 19 October 2026, the owner reported checking
the independent challenge statement with the Japanese reading guide
and confirming that it expresses the paper's classification claim
(P006-15). This is a human check of the statement's meaning,
not human peer review of the proof, a new machine equivalence proof,
or a novelty review. Human proof peer review and novelty relative to
the full position-mapping theory remain outstanding.
The historical 41 arithmetic lemmas and four conditional/prototype
entries are retained with their exact types in the 57-claim inventory.
Their count is not a percentage of formalization; they are no longer
the frontier of the supplied formal development.

\section{Formal graph and proved conclusions}\label{sec:lean}
The graph specification uses twenty oriented parent faces on twelve
labels, integer lattice points of closed triangles, and equivalence
generated by edge gluings. The simple graph \record{gcGraph} defines
adjacency from lattice triangles. Its \record{LiteralPath} uses actual
neighbour sets, distinct vertices and an even vertex count, permitting
internal degree-five vertices. The predicate \record{criterion}
includes primitivity and the alternatives in (2), on natural inputs
$0<l<k$.

Proved graph isomorphisms connect the surface descriptions to this
quotient, retaining ordinary parent-edge vertices in the nonprimitive
case. Degree five is equivalent to being a parent vertex; other vertices
have degree six. The argument derives local triangle continuation,
coherent chart changes and a finite lift of every literal path.
Primitive necessity uses start reduction and sector collisions;
positive constructions give the converse. The full theorem is
\[
 (\exists n,p,\ \operatorname{LiteralPath}(\operatorname{gcGraph}(k,l),n,p))
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{criterion}(k,l).
\]
There is no primitivity hypothesis. For Corollary~\ref{cor:minimum},
the formal bounded arithmetic theorem shows that among primitive
$k>l>0$ with $T\le399$, absence is equivalent to $(k,l)=(17,5)$.
Its supporting lemmas prove absence, existence below the bound,
primitivity and the norm calculation.

For Corollary~\ref{cor:rays}, the formal arithmetic result supplies a
threshold and positive period on every eventually interior integer
affine ray. The full classification transports it to actual path
existence, including nonprimitive points. A natural ray parameter
describes the same positive tail as sufficiently large integer time.
The prose argument above gives the effective arithmetic construction;
the formal result has existence scope. Auxiliary claim identifiers
below refer to their exact typed statements in the claim ledger.

\subsection{Parameter checks and path audits}
An explicit graph constructor and literal-path checker test the
classification on 123 primitive pairs through $T=673$: 116 positive
and seven negative. A discovery set through $T=5000$ has 921 points,
602 positive and 319 negative. Further fixed predictions include
sets of twenty, fourteen, forty-six and thirty points; all decisions
match. The forty-six-point range is $9049\le T\le185851$ and the
thirty-point maximum is $T=488721$. A separately constructed comparison
of 360 pairs with $5000<T\le7000$ has 171 positive and 189 negative
decisions; twenty-six were known, leaving 334 new inputs.

Two arithmetic implementations agree at cutoffs $10^4,10^5,10^6,10^7$.
At $X=10^7$ there are 1,837,762 primitive points, 81,946 positive and
1,755,816 negative (about 95.54\%). These are finite arithmetic counts.
Direct endpoint formulas agree with unit continuation on 161 unit-residue,
76 second-stage and 323 assembled paths, totalling 560 paths with
repeated graphs.

The finite belt audit checks eight belts, twenty caps and 337 endpoint
orders (159 outer, 63 second positive fan, 68 first positive fan,
47 folded second). It checks every vertex, cut triangle piece and cut
on 160 known negative graphs and 320 starts, and all 19,200 starts
of those same graphs. Nine rays have 1,809 arithmetic comparisons and
fourteen graph instances. The aggregate workload is 286,940 vertices,
286,300 triangles, 303,857 pieces and 19,412 cuts; these counts overlap
the examples rather than enlarging their number.

A separate constructor checks 191 theorem-domain pairs with $T\le700$:
127 primitive (120 positive, seven negative) and 64 nonprimitive,
all negative. Another 39 nonprimitive boundary pairs consist of
25 $(k,0)$ and 14 $(k,k)$ inputs. Two controls $(1,0),(1,1)$ give
232 stored records in total. All decisions agree, including minimum
$T=399$; positive paths and 13,200 negative-start certificates are
checked. The boundary pairs are outside Theorem~\ref{thm:classification}.

The IPR census has a separate full-canonical-code-set comparison on
64 even sizes $C_{60}$--$C_{186}$, with 43,636,843 outputs per generator
and 346 negatives. The full $C_{60}$--$C_{200}$ totals and the scope of
their decision and certificate checks are given in Appendix~\ref{app:census}.

\subsection{Current status of the claims}
The definition, two start orbits, and candidate endpoints have been
checked against the source and in AI prose review, but lack a complete
formal surface connection at that historical checkpoint. The main AR positive argument was reviewed;
its finite belt and cap tables were checked later. Through the fixed
review \record{9fedf3fc}, the coordinator checked congruence exclusion,
endpoint ordering, the positive-side A calculations, outer A coordinates,
negative-side A regions, the collision identities, and their period
differences. Ownership of all outer A pieces and some negative-side A
lower bounds retained abbreviated steps. The periodic transfer of the
finite tables was rederived. Signs, small widths, simplicity, and degrees
were checked, while some full cap-piece arguments remained partial.
Appendices B and C explicitly supply B's three regions and the terminal
caps. A later fixed review, \record{49430e1c} (03:46 JST, 19 October
2026), records the coordinator's recalculation of all formulas in the
Japanese v4 Appendices B and C, with no missing steps found. This review
was omitted from English v6's status metadata. English v6.2 corrects the
omission; it transcribes the Japanese proof, with the coordinator's
separate machine checks of selected English formulas recorded in P006.
The later addendum \record{c1b27f1d}, headed 15:10 JST, completes
the general AI prose review of A-sheet items 2 and 3: Appendix C
supplies the terminal containment, and the diagonal-A initial cap
was rederived in that addendum. P006-11 records this update.
The English-v5 review addendum \record{f88d1b6a} identifies its one
failed check as the R004 nonprimitive domain count corrected in
P006-09; the other 76 checks passed. The typesetting issue was
outside those 77 checks. Neither addendum supplies human peer
review, full formalization, or an independent necessity proof; the later
R004 receipt below supplies the last of these separately.

P006-13 records two independently derived general prose proofs of
the entire classification: the research team's proof and R004's
alternative. R004 knew the claim but did not read the main proof,
construction or code. One AI coordinator reviewed both directions;
this is not human peer review. P006-14 adds the full Lean theorem
and the primitive minimum, and records the full-theorem Comparator
acceptance. Thus \record{thm:classification} and \record{cor:minimum}
are \texttt{lean-proved} for the exact independent graph statements,
while novelty and human proof review remain separate obligations.
P006-15 records the owner's statement-meaning confirmation without
promoting the proof to human-reviewed. Ray
periodicity has a formal existence theorem; effective threshold and
period computation remains uncertified. Density retains its general
counting review obligations. These updates do not extend the separate
dated census receipt boundary in Section 10.3.
